about: Metro structure gauge (Ben, 27-28 October 2026; claude/Metro_Structure_Gauge_Handoff.md). Drawing values. Read by the Rail Profiles editor, the Mill Creek Deck and Station 3D; edit on the hub page.

A.label: type A tube (cast iron, bench walls)

grades.note: By building phase (Ben, 29 October): 5% everywhere; Phases 1-2 straight underground up to 6% as a warning; after Phase 2 (Phase 3 on) up to 6% on a straight; after Phase 3 (later) also up to 6% on curves over 500 m (train-averaged radius); above 6% always an error. Straight: train-averaged radius at least straight_radius.

phases_about: Per phase (Ben, 28 October; tunnel methods by era): cc_max is the deepest cut and cover (rail depth, m); min_drive the shortest shield drive (m; a judgement, not sourced); deep_from the rail depth of lift or escalator stations. Shield needs one tube diameter of cover over the crown: type A from 10.10 m, the bore from 15.50 m, type C from 10.85 m. Phase 1 cc_max 12.19 m (40 ft, the canon-shallow flag); Phase 2 16.5 m (the bore minimum + 1 m, so the methods overlap); Phase 3 15 m.
min_radius_about: Metro minimum horizontal radius (m) for station approaches and spacing changes: a drawing value from the track geometry handoff's example (28 October), not Ben's; set it on the hub page.
tbm_about: phases.tbm (Ben, 31 October: "deep-bore is a thing when it's TBM"): running tunnels and mined stations of a phase with tbm are the deep bore by tunnel boring machine, else the hand shield. Phase 3 and later by default (drawing values; set on the hub page).
hall_about: Station halls (Station_Access_and_Mezzanines_by_Phase, 31 October; drawing values): a ticket hall or mezzanine sits on the box roof: clear height 2.75 m (Piccadilly Circus 9 ft), its roof slab 0.6 m, cover over it 0.6 m. The least rail depth for a hall, D_HALL, is the box's rail-to-roof-top (4.6 m side, 5.2 m island) plus these: 8.55 m side, 9.15 m island.
subway_streets_about: Streets built over the subway (Ben, 31 October): Central Parkway, Victory Parkway and MLK were laid out over the cut-and-cover box, so a box under them is built with the street. Matched by name (any part); marked on the profile as 'built over the subway'.
cost_about: cost.cover_hard: the fraction of a diameter of cover below which a tube cannot be bored at all (unbuildable); between that and a full diameter it is bored with ground treatment (a warning). The cost sums of 1 November (box, bore, switch, treatment per metre) are gone with the per-stretch engine (4 November): the method is a decision by rule, not a cost comparison.
portal_min_about: An open run inside a tunnel shorter than this is tunnelled through, not a portal: a train cannot surface and go back under in less (the ramps at the grade limit), 1 November.
paint_fit_about: A paint or a station's type holds only where its structure can be built at the drawn rail on the finished ground (Ben, 2 November: the painting has to make sense): a box's roof under the ground, an open trough's rail under the ground and no deeper than cc_max, at grade within the box's height below and a viaduct's height above the ground, elevated with the deck's underside over the ground, a mined station with the hard cover of its tube. Elsewhere it is unbuildable (hatched), with Lower, Raise or Clear. A paint does not raise the ground (Ben, 3 November): the regraded ground is drawn on the Profiles page (Ground, like a rail profile: points, straight grades, the ends on the ground), and Propose fill draws the fill a box or tube needs as a line to edit; a tube short of one diameter of cover is a warning.
elevated_station_about: Ben, 2 November 2026: an elevated station type with a mezzanine / passthrough under it. The mezzanine is at street level under the middle of the platforms (fare control, stairs up to each platform) and open across the line as a public passage. mezzanine_clear_m is its clear height to the underside of the platform deck (deckDepth under the rail): the rail stands at least deckDepth + mezzanine_clear_m over the ground. A starting value, not a ruling.
prefer_about: phases.prefer (Ben, 4 November): the method of an unpainted stretch between anchors where both cut and cover (within cc_max throughout) and a bored drive (full cover between its launch boxes, at least min_drive) can be built: cutcover or bored. Phase 1 cut and cover, as American practice was (tunnelling only where digging was blocked); Phases 2 and 3 bored (Chicago 1943: shield between cut-and-cover stations). Set on the hub page.
